nodes.name: Property B
nodes.statement: A hypergraph is said to have property B if there exists a proper subset $\textit{S}$ of its vertices such that every hyperedge of the hypergraph contains vertices from both $\textit{S}$ and $\textit{$\overline{S}$}$, the complement of $S$. In other words, if the vertices of a hypergraph can be colored using Red and Blue colors such that every hyperedge of the hypergraph contains Red as well as Blue vertices, then that hypergraph is said to have {\it Property B}.
nodes.statement_short: A hypergraph has Property B iff its vertices admit a Red/Blue coloring leaving no hyperedge monochromatic.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.origin_citation: Erdos and Hajnal (classical); cf. Lovasz, Combinatorial Problems and Exercises

nodes.statement_short: $H'$ is the $n$-CNF containing, for each hyperedge, the all-positive clause and the all-negated clause on its vertices.

nodes.name: Index subsets $U_K$ and $V_K$
nodes.statement: For any $K = \{a_1, a_2, \ldots a_k\}$ which is a proper subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ such that $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 \ldots < a_k \leq n$, we denote $U_K = \{u_{a_1}, u_{a_2}, \ldots, u_{a_k}\}$ and $V_K = \{v_{a_1}, v_{a_2}, \ldots, v_{a_k}\}$. We also define ${\bar{U}}_K = U \setminus U_K$ and ${\bar{V}}_K = V \setminus V_K$.

nodes.name: The ordered set $V^p$
nodes.statement: Let $V^1 = (v_1, v_2, v_3, \ldots, v_n)$ denote the ordered set where $v_1 \prec v_2 \ldots \prec v_n$. For any $1 \leq p \leq n$, let $v_1^p=v_p$, $v_p^1 = v_1$ and $v_j^j = v_j$ for all $j \neq 1,p$. Let $V^p$ be the ordered set formed after swapping $v_1$ and $v_p$ of $V^1$. Then, $V^p = (v_1^p, v_2,\ldots, v_{p-1},v_p^1,v_{p+1} \ldots v_n)$ where $v_1^p \prec v_2^p \ldots \prec v_n^p$.
nodes.statement_short: $V^p$ is the ordered vertex set obtained from $V^1$ by swapping $v_1$ and $v_p$.

nodes.name: matching pair in the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$)
nodes.statement: Consider one particular ordered set $V^p$. For each $1 \leq i \leq n$, we call $u_i \in U$ and $v_i^p \in V^p$ to be a {\it matching pair} of vertices in the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$).

nodes.statement: Similarly, for any $Q = \{a_1, a_2, \ldots a_q\}$ which is a proper subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n-2\}$ such that $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 \ldots < a_q \leq n-2$, we denote $U'_Q = \{u'_{a_1}, u'_{a_2}, \ldots, u'_{a_q}\}$ and $V'_Q = \{v'_{a_1}, v'_{a_2}, \ldots, v'_{a_q}\}$. We also define ${\bar{U'}}_Q = U' \setminus U'_Q$ and ${\bar{V'}}_Q = V' \setminus V'_Q$.

nodes.name: The ingredient hypergraphs $A$, $B$ and $C$ of the $m(8)$ construction
nodes.statement: Let $A =(V_1, E_1)$ be a non-$2$-colorable $5$-uniform hypergraph that produces the best known upper bound for $m(5)$. Let $E_1 = \{ e^A_1, e^A_2, e^A_3, \ldots, e^A_{m(5)} \}$. Let $B =(V_2, E_2)$ be a Fano plane \cite{klein} such that the set of hyperedges is $E_2 = \{ e^B_1, e^B_2, e^B_3, \ldots, e^B_{m(3)} \}$. Let $C =(V_3, E_3)$ be another Fano plane \cite{klein} such that the set of hyperedges is $E_3 = \{ e^C_1, e^C_2, e^C_3, \ldots, e^C_{m(3)} \}$.

nodes.name: Result 1
nodes.statement: We provide a construction which shows that $m(n) \leq (n+1) \cdot 2^{n-2} + \linebreak (n-1) \cdot m(n-2)$ when $n$ is odd, and $m(n) \leq (n+1) \cdot 2^{n-2} + {n \choose {n / 2}}/{2} + (n-1) \cdot \left( m(n-2) + {n-2 \choose {(n-2)}/{2}} \right)$ when $n$ is even.
nodes.statement_short: A construction giving improved parity-dependent recurrences for $m(n)$ with leading term $(n+1)2^{n-2}$.

nodes.name: Abbott-Moser composite construction
nodes.statement: Let us discuss their construction in brief. Take an $a$-uniform hypergraph giving the best known value for $m(a)$ and replace the vertices of this hypergraph with different $b$-uniform hypergraphs that gives the best known value for $m(b)$. Note that the vertex set of each of these $b$-uniform hypergraphs must be disjoint from each other. In order to form an $n$-uniform hyperedge, the hyperedges of these $a$ different $b$-uniform hypergraphs are combined with each other in every possible way. Therefore, the $n$-uniform hypergraph has a total of $m(a) \cdot (m(b))^a$ hyperedges.
nodes.statement_short: Blow up each vertex of an optimal $a$-uniform hypergraph into a disjoint optimal $b$-uniform hypergraph and combine hyperedges in all possible ways.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

different $b$-uniform hypergraphs that gives the best known value for $m(b)$
output: the $n$-uniform hypergraph has a total of $m(a) \cdot (m(b))^a$ hyperedges

nodes.name: AHT construction
nodes.statement: Let us now define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $X \cup U \cup V$, and the following hyperedges are present in $H$:\\ $(i)$ $\{u_i\} \cup e_j \cup \{v_i\}$ for every pair of $i, j$ satisfying $1 \leq i \leq n$ and $1 \leq j \leq m_{n-2}$. $(ii)$ $U$ $(iii)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. $(iv)$ $V_K \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine each matching pair $(u_i,v_i)$ with every core hyperedge, then add $U$ and the parity-selected sets $U_K \cup \bar{V}_K$ and $V_K \cup \bar{U}_K$.

nodes.name: First improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement: Now we define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $X \cup U \cup V$, and the set of hyperedges is the following:\\ $(i)$ $\{u_i\} \cup e_j \cup \{v_i\}$ for every pair of $i, j$ satisfying $2 \leq i \leq n$ and $1 \leq j \leq m_{n-2}$. $(ii)$ $U$ $(iii)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}^p_K}$ for every $1 \leq p \leq n$ and every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. $(iv)$ $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $1 \leq p \leq n$ and every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.statement_short: Same as AHT but skipping the pair $(u_1,v_1)$ on the core and iterating steps (iii)-(iv) over all $n$ swapped orderings $V^p$.

nodes.name: Further improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement: Let us now define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $X \cup U \cup V \cup U' \cup V'$, and the following hyperedges are present in $H$:\\ $(i)$ $\{u'_i\} \cup e_j \cup \{v'_i\}$ for every pair of $i, j$ satisfying $1 \leq i \leq n-2$ and $1 \leq j \leq m_{n-2}$. $(ii)$ $U' \cup \{u_i\} \cup \{v_i\}$, for each $i$ satisfying $1 \leq i \leq n$. $(iii)$ $U'_Q \cup {\bar{V'}}_Q \cup \{u_i\} \cup \{v_i\}$ for every $Q$ and $i$ such that $|Q|$ is odd, $1 \leq |Q| \leq \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor$ and $1 \leq i \leq n$. $(iv)$ $V'_Q \cup {\bar{U'}}_Q \cup \{u_i\} \cup \{v_i\}$ for every $Q$ and $i$ such that $|Q|$ is even, $2 \leq |Q| \leq \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor$ and $1 \leq i \leq n$. $(v)$ $U$ $(vi)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. $(vii)$ $V_K \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.statement_short: Insert an auxiliary $(n-2)$-level AHT gadget on $U',V'$ between the core hypergraph and the top-level AHT gadget on $U,V$.

nodes.name: Construction of an $8$-uniform hypergraph with $1269$ hyperedges
nodes.statement: Let us now define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $8$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $U \cup V \cup V_1 \cup V_2 \cup V_3$, and the following hyperedges are present in $H$:\\ $(i)$ $ e^A_j \cup e^B_l $ for every $j$ and $l$ satisfying $1 \leq j \leq m(5)$ and $1 \leq l \leq m(3)$. $(ii)$ $ e^A_j \cup e^C_{l'} $ for every $j$ and $l'$ satisfying $1 \leq j \leq m(5)$ and $1 \leq l' \leq m(3)$. $(iii)$ $ \{u_i\} \cup e^B_l \cup e^C_{l'} \cup \{v_i\} $ for every $i$, $l$ and $l'$ satisfying $1 \leq i \leq 8$, $1 \leq l, l' \leq m(3)$. $(iv)$ $U$ $(v)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq 3$. $(vi)$ $V_K \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Glue an optimal $5$-uniform hypergraph to two Fano planes and cap with the AHT gadget on $U,V$, giving $m(8) \leq 1269$.

nodes.name: Proof of the matching-pair coloring lemma
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that there is no \textit{matching pair} ($u_i,v_i^p$) in the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i^p$ are colored by Red. Let $U_K$ denote the set of vertices in $U$ which are Red in this coloring, where $K \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots n\}$ denotes the set of indices of the vertices in the set $U_K$. Note that $U_K$ must be a proper subset of $U$, as $U$ is one of the hyperedges of $H$. Let us consider the following $2$ cases: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Case 1: $1 \leq |U_K| < \lfloor n/2\rfloor$} If $|U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $|U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. \item \textbf{Case 2: $\lfloor n/2\rfloor \leq |U_K| < n$} If $n - |U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $n - |U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored by Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction, splitting on the size of the Red set $U_K$ and exhibiting a monochromatic hyperedge in each case.

nodes.name: Proof of non-$2$-colorability of the first improved construction
nodes.statement: Consider a Red-Blue coloring $\chi$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the \textit{core hypergraph} $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that the pair ($u_1,v_1$) is not combined with any hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph} to form a hyperedge. It can also be noted that any other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, is combined with every hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph}, and therefore both $u_i$ and $v_i$ cannot be colored by Red. \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Case 1:} If either of $u_1$ or $v_1$ is colored with Blue, then there is no pair ($u_i,v_i$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i$ are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$. \item \textbf{Case 2:} If both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices ($u_i,v_i$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$. \item \textbf{Case 3:} Let us assume that both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red, and there exists at least one other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue. Consider the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^i$). It can be noted that there does not exist any \textit{matching pair} of vertices ($u_j,v_j^i$) in ($U,V^i$) such that both $u_j$ and $v_j^i$ are colored with Red. Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.$\;\;\;\;$\qed
nodes.statement_short: Assume the core is Red, then in each of three cases select an ordering $V^p$ satisfying the hypothesis of the matching-pair lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of non-$2$-colorability of the further improved construction
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable core hypergraph $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that none of the matching pair of vertices $u'_i$ and $v'_i$, $1 \leq i \leq (n-2)$, can have both their colors as Red as it causes a contradiction to our assumption due to Step $(i )$ of the construction. Therefore, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that at least one of the $(n-2)$-uniform sets formed in the Steps $(ii), (iii)$ and $(iv)$ (after excluding the vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$) of the construction must be monochromatic under the given coloring $\chi$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that it is monochromatic in Blue. Then, none of the matching pair of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$, can have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$ as it causes a contradiction to our assumption. Then, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in Steps $(v), (vi)$ and $(vii)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction, applying the $p=1$ case of the matching-pair lemma twice: first to the auxiliary $U',V'$ gadget, then to the top-level $U,V$ gadget.

nodes.name: Proof of non-$2$-colorability of the $8$-uniform construction
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable $5$-uniform hypergraph $A$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$ and let $e^A_j \in E_1$ be the hyperedge that is monochromatic in Red. It can be noted from Step $(i)$ of the construction that the non-$2$-colorable $3$-uniform hypergraph $B$ must contain a hyperedge $e^B_l \in E_2$ which is monochromatic in Blue. Similarly, it can be seen from Step $(ii)$ of the construction that the non-$2$-colorable $3$-uniform hypergraph $C$ contains a hyperedge $e^C_{l'} \in E_3$ which is monochromatic in Blue. Since both the hyperedges $e^B_l$ and $e^C_{l'}$ are Blue, it follows from Step $(iii)$ that any of the \textit{matching pair} of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $u_i \in U$, $v_i \in V$, $1 \leq i \leq 8$, cannot have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$. It follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in the Steps $(iv), (v)$ and $(vi)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a Red hyperedge of $A$ forces Blue hyperedges in both Fano planes, which forces the matching-pair hypothesis and hence a monochromatic hyperedge.

All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $n - |U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored by Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. \qed
nodes.statement_short: For a large Red set, the same two parity sub-cases again produce an all-Blue hyperedge.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Assume the core hypergraph is Red
nodes.statement: Consider a Red-Blue coloring $\chi$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the \textit{core hypergraph} $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that the pair ($u_1,v_1$) is not combined with any hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph} to form a hyperedge. It can also be noted that any other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, is combined with every hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph}, and therefore both $u_i$ and $v_i$ cannot be colored by Red.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG the core is monochromatic Red, so no pair $(u_i,v_i)$ with $i \neq 1$ is all-Red.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Case 1: $u_1$ or $v_1$ is Blue
nodes.statement: \item \textbf{Case 1:} If either of $u_1$ or $v_1$ is colored with Blue, then there is no pair ($u_i,v_i$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i$ are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: No all-Red pair exists, so the matching-pair lemma applies to $(U,V^1)$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Case 2: $(u_1,v_1)$ Red and no all-Blue pair
nodes.statement: \item \textbf{Case 2:} If both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices ($u_i,v_i$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: The hypothesis of the matching-pair lemma again holds for $(U,V^1)$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Case 3: $(u_1,v_1)$ Red and some pair $(u_i,v_i)$ Blue
nodes.statement: \item \textbf{Case 3:} Let us assume that both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red, and there exists at least one other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue. Consider the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^i$). It can be noted that there does not exist any \textit{matching pair} of vertices ($u_j,v_j^i$) in ($U,V^i$) such that both $u_j$ and $v_j^i$ are colored with Red. Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.$\;\;\;\;$\qed
nodes.statement_short: Switch to the ordering $V^i$, where no matching pair is all-Red, and apply the lemma.

nodes.name: Assume the core is Red; no auxiliary pair is all-Red
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable core hypergraph $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that none of the matching pair of vertices $u'_i$ and $v'_i$, $1 \leq i \leq (n-2)$, can have both their colors as Red as it causes a contradiction to our assumption due to Step $(i )$ of the construction.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the contradiction and rule out all-Red matching pairs $(u'_i,v'_i)$ via Step (i).
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Apply the $p=1$ lemma to the auxiliary gadget
nodes.statement: Therefore, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that at least one of the $(n-2)$-uniform sets formed in the Steps $(ii), (iii)$ and $(iv)$ (after excluding the vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$) of the construction must be monochromatic under the given coloring $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: The matching-pair lemma forces one $(n-2)$-uniform set of Steps (ii)-(iv) to be monochromatic.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Rule out all-Blue matching pairs $(u_i,v_i)$
nodes.statement: Without the loss of generality, let us assume that it is monochromatic in Blue. Then, none of the matching pair of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$, can have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$ as it causes a contradiction to our assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Taking that set Blue, no top-level matching pair can be all-Blue.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Apply the $p=1$ lemma to the top-level gadget and conclude
nodes.statement: Then, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in Steps $(v), (vi)$ and $(vii)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: The lemma then yields a monochromatic hyperedge among Steps (v)-(vii), a contradiction.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Assume a Red hyperedge in $A$
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable $5$-uniform hypergraph $A$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$ and let $e^A_j \in E_1$ be the hyperedge that is monochromatic in Red.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the contradiction and fix an all-Red hyperedge $e^A_j$ of $A$.

nodes.name: Step (i) forces a Blue hyperedge in $B$
nodes.statement: It can be noted from Step $(i)$ of the construction that the non-$2$-colorable $3$-uniform hypergraph $B$ must contain a hyperedge $e^B_l \in E_2$ which is monochromatic in Blue.
nodes.statement_short: The unions $e^A_j \cup e^B_l$ force some Fano hyperedge of $B$ to be all-Blue.

nodes.name: Step (ii) forces a Blue hyperedge in $C$
nodes.statement: Similarly, it can be seen from Step $(ii)$ of the construction that the non-$2$-colorable $3$-uniform hypergraph $C$ contains a hyperedge $e^C_{l'} \in E_3$ which is monochromatic in Blue.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrically, some Fano hyperedge of $C$ is all-Blue.
nodes.section: 5 A construction that improves the upper bound for m(8)

nodes.name: Step (iii) rules out all-Blue matching pairs
nodes.statement: Since both the hyperedges $e^B_l$ and $e^C_{l'}$ are Blue, it follows from Step $(iii)$ that any of the \textit{matching pair} of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $u_i \in U$, $v_i \in V$, $1 \leq i \leq 8$, cannot have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: With both Fano hyperedges Blue, no matching pair $(u_i,v_i)$ can be all-Blue.

nodes.name: Apply the $p=1$ lemma and conclude
nodes.statement: It follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in the Steps $(iv), (v)$ and $(vi)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: The matching-pair lemma gives a monochromatic hyperedge among Steps (iv)-(vi), a contradiction.
